scenario: AITA for wanting my girlfriend to be less braggy about her work perks? She seems to forget that the way she lives isn't how most people live... | My girlfriend has a pretty sweet job. She doesn't have set hours; she just has to work 35 hours a week whenever is convenient for her and make it to her few meetings. She can work from the office or from home sometimes. She has a full benefits package despite being under what most people consider full time. A really nice retirement package too. And the company will pay everything for continued education. She does work she finds interesting (cutting edge robotics) and gets along well with her coworkers. She has a lot of PTO per year and her boss even lets the employees "earn up" more; if they work extra hours one week they can ask for the equivalent in PTO for later. Her team's managers buy them whatever they want for the office; they want a 500 dollar expresso maker, they get it. They want a type of fancy coffee, they get it. Nice furniture, done... They get paid well too; pretty middle of the road salary for robotics but she says the work life balance more than makes up for it. She'd rather have more time than be a top earner. And honestly a midrange robotics salary is still damn good. And anyway, For a while I thought "good for her" for having found something that she is happy with. But recently it's gotten frustrating because I think she forgets that this isn't how everyone lives. Like when we're out with my friends or just hanging out she'll talk about the nice stuff her managers bought for the office, about all the vacations she takes, about how she and her coworkers left the office in the middle of the day to see a movie then came back and just worked a little later. And yeah, it seems like she forgets that is no way a normal job. So last night we were at a party and she mentioned how she was going to tour a few new apartments Monday morning and afternoon, and one of the people at the party was like "don't you have work" and she said "yeah but I can set my own hours" And that just rubbed me the wrong way and I said that she needed to stop going on and on about her work perks, it was obnoxious and came off braggy. She was like "I was just explaining something" and I said it wasn't just this, it was everything. Most people don't live the life she lives." She said that I was coming off jealous and that it was a bad look. That she was where she was because she didn't settle for less; she studied and worked her ass off, and didn't let herself get too settled anywhere she was unfulfilled. And that instead of complaining, maybe I should ask myself what I'm feeling jealous of and what I need to do to get it. I told her she was missing the point; she'll always be around people who don't have what she does, and she could be a little more modest about it. She said I was the only one who seemed to have a problem with it, and stormed off... AITA for what I said?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being AITA (A Guy In Trouble) for wanting my girlfriend to be less braggy about her work perks. Let me break this down step by step. First, I need to understand the situation. My girlfriend has a really sweet job with a lot of perks. She has flexible hours, can work from home, has a good benefits package, nice retirement plan, paid time off, and even gets to have nice office amenities like an espresso maker and fancy furniture. She's happy with her job, and I initially thought that was great for her. But lately, it's been frustrating because she seems to forget that not everyone has such a great job. When we're out with friends or just hanging out, she talks about her job perks a lot. For example, she mentioned that she was going to tour apartments during the day on Monday, and someone asked if she had work, and she said she could set her own hours. That rubbed me the wrong way because I felt like she was bragging about her job perks. I told her she needed to stop going on and on about it because it was obnoxious and came off as braggy. She responded by saying she was just explaining something and that I was being jealous. She pointed out that she worked hard to get where she is and that she didn't settle for less. She suggested I should ask myself what I'm feeling jealous of and what I need to do to get it. I told her she was missing the point and that she should be more modest because she'll always be around people who don't have what she does. She said I was the only one with a problem and stormed off. Now, I'm wondering if I'm AITA for what I said. Let me think about this. On one hand, I can see why I'm frustrated. Not everyone has such a great job, and it's easy to feel like she's flaunting her perks, especially when others might be struggling. It's natural to feel a bit jealous or resentful when she's talking about her job in a way that seems to ignore the reality that most people don't have that kind of flexibility or benefits. On the other hand, she worked hard to get her job, and she's entitled to be proud of her achievements. She's not bragging; she's just sharing her experiences. It's possible that I'm projecting my own insecurities onto her. Maybe I'm feeling jealous because I don't have a job like hers, and that's making me react negatively when she talks about it. I also need to consider how I approached the conversation. I told her she was being obnoxious and braggy, which might have come off as accusatory. Instead, maybe I should have expressed my feelings more gently, explaining how her talking about her job makes me feel. That way, she might be more understanding instead of feeling attacked. Another angle is to think about the dynamics of our relationship. If she's the only one who's successful in her job, maybe I'm feeling insecure about my own situation. It's important to communicate openly about these feelings without making her feel bad for her achievements. I also wonder if there's a middle ground. Maybe she can be more mindful of how often she talks about her job perks, especially in social settings where others might not have the same experiences. But at the same time, she shouldn't have to suppress her pride in her job just to make me feel better. In the end, I think the key is communication. I need to express my feelings without making her feel attacked, and she needs to understand that my frustration isn't about her job but about how it makes me feel in comparison to others. If we can have an open and honest conversation, we might find a way to balance her enthusiasm with my feelings of jealousy. So, considering all this, I think I might be AITA because I didn't approach the conversation in the best way. Instead of expressing my feelings, I criticized her, which led to an argument. However, I also think it's valid to feel frustrated when she seems unaware of how her job perks compare to others. It's a tricky situation, and both of us need to work on communication to resolve it.
